gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 13 build now compiles both the landed libfs starter tests and the new reviewability gate so the helper lane stays honest as it grows.
The existing make target keeps the bounded libfs starter and reviewability checks runnable through the same repeatable path as the other Zigux tranche checkpoints.

The landed starter already mirrors the pure helper-facing shape of simple_statfs(), always_delete_dentry(), and simple_lookup() without claiming live dcache mutation, inode locking, or VFS registration.
Dedicated starter tests keep the current wrapper honest around split fsid packing, default statfs values, negative-dentry discard intent, casefold passthrough, and name-length rejection.
The slice note records the narrow boundary of the landed helper lab so the lane does not overstate itself as live libfs or VFS parity.
A dedicated reviewability gate ties the current starter, tests, slice note, and survey note together so future runs can confirm the lane state before widening helper coverage.
The survey note now describes the landed starter truthfully and keeps the remaining gap around directory iteration, offset policy, and deeper VFS state explicit.

The next honest step is one small directory-reading or offset-policy helper around dcache_readdir() or the early offset surface, keeping the work cursor-free and in-memory before any live dentries, inode state, or pseudo-filesystem plumbing is attempted.
